newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Year-end results send Kuwait index soaring.
newsitem.headline: Year-end results send Kuwait index soaring.

text.p: The Kuwait share index rose 74.7 points to 1,975.1 record high at the end of the week to Wednesday as "good" year-end profits for listed firms fuelled demand, analysts said on Thursday.
"Dealers are encouraged by the annual results of (listed) firms. The results so far have been very good," said an analyst.
"People are buying shares of firms they expect will announce high profits," he added.
Losers led gainers 36-9, while eight did not move, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday showed.

The daily average for value of traded shares rose to 25.1 million dinars ($83.1 million) during the five-day week from 18.5 million. Volume increased to a daily average of 81.7 million shares from 65.1 million.
"Had it not been Ramadan (the Moselm fasting month) trade could have been even more active," said an analyst. Trade traditionally eases during Ramadan which ends in the first third of February.
Nonetheless, "I expect the market to be stronger in the coming weeks," he said.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 41.6 million dinars, followed by banks with 28.1 million and services firms with 14.7 million.
Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Securities House, The International Investor, Kuwait Real Estate, Public Warehousing and Mobile Telecommunications were among the most traded shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
